title: Security & Compliance — Integrated Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows
author: Maya Patel
short_intro: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational security controls and compliance workflows across RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident-response security procedures, compliance evidence collection, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for engineers, security reviewers, and compliance owners who operate or evaluate production inference infrastructure.
scope: Applies to all hosted, dedicated, and private deployments managed by Redwood Inference and third-party infrastructure where Redwood systems process or store customer data. Excludes purely experimental prototypes in private developer sandboxes unless they are promoted to a staging or production environment.
ownership_and_contacts: Owner team: security; Primary author: Maya Patel (Security Engineering); Security On-Call: security-oncall@redwood.ai; Compliance Manager: Liam O'Connor; Infra Lead: Jenna Rivera
rbac_and_authentication: Goals: Enforce least privilege across control plane and data plane components. Prefer role-based access with centralized identity provider (IdP) integrations and short-lived credentials. Policies: 1) IdP: All interactive user authentication must use the corporate SSO (SAML 2.0 / OIDC) with mandatory MFA. 2) Service accounts: Use short-lived workload identities (OIDC or IAM roles) where possible; service account keys are forbidden unless approved by security. 3) RBAC model: Roles defined: admin, operator, developer, auditor, viewer. Role bindings scoped by resource tag (customer-id, env:prod/stage/dev) and business unit. 4) Privileged access reviews: Quarterly attestations for all admin and operator role assignments. Implementation checklist: Centralize groups in IdP and sync to the access management service; Enforce just-in-time (JIT) elevation for sensitive operations via approval workflow; Log all privilege grant/revoke events to audit logging pipeline.
audit_logging: Requirements: Collect and retain logs for authentication, authorization, deployment actions, model loads, cache evictions, admin CLI usage, API policy decisions, and data-access events. Central log sinks: Splunk (primary), S3 (long-term cold store), and Elasticsearch (short-term search). All logs must be cryptographically signed and written with KMS-backed server-side encryption. Retention and tiers: Hot index (Elasticsearch): 90 days. Warm/Archive (Splunk/S3): 7 years for regulated customers or as contractually required; 1 year default for non-regulated customers. Logging fields (minimum): timestamp, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_id, resource_type, outcome (allow/deny/error), request_id, trace_id, region, deployment_env. Operational notes: Ensure high-cardinality keys are avoided for hot indices. Configure alerts on audit-forwarding failures (S3 write errors, Kinesis/Firehose throttles).
data_residency_and_retention: Residency model: Data at rest must be stored only in approved regions per customer contract. Default hosted regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1. Private deployments honor customer-managed regions and network boundaries. Classification and retention table: Data class | Example | Default retention; Auth logs | IdP events | 1 year; Audit logs | Admin/API audits | 7 years (regulated)/1 year (default); Customer data | Model inputs/outputs | Customer-configurable (default 30 days); Metrics/telemetry | Aggregated usage | 3 years (aggregated). Encryption & key management: Production data must use KMS-managed keys (cloud KMS or HSM for private deployments). Key rotation: annual rotation for data keys; re-encrypt per rotation window.
secure_sdlc_and_development_controls: Principles: Shift-left security: automated scanning and gating in CI, dependency management, and threat modeling for design reviews. Mandatory controls: 1) Static analysis (SAST) in CI for all services; fail build on high/critical findings unless mitigated with an accepted risk exception. 2) Dependency scanning (SCA) and license checks; vulnerable direct dependencies must be remediated within SLA (30 days for critical, 90 days for high). 3) Secret scanning and prevention in pre-commit hooks and CI; secrets in commits trigger automated revocation and incident creation. 4) Pull-request protection: require at least one security review on changes touching security-sensitive components (auth, encryption, logging, deployment pipelines). 5) Container/image hardening: base images must be from approved catalogs and scanned; ephemeral runtime policies enforced by sandboxing. Release controls: Canary rollouts with automatic rollback on error rate or SLA breach. Release checklist must include audit log verification and access-control changes review.
incident_response_security_procedures: Objectives: Rapid containment, evidence preservation, and coordinated communications with customers and regulators when required. Detection & Triage: 1) Alerts from monitoring or third-party reports flow into PagerDuty with predefined playbooks. 2) Initial triage must capture attacker-surface (affected services, impacted customer IDs, timeline) within first 60 minutes. Containment & Eradication: Short-term: revoke compromised credentials, isolate affected instances/pods, disable ingresses where necessary. Medium-term: rotate keys, rebuild images from known-good sources, apply mitigations across fleet. Forensics & Evidence Preservation: Preserve raw audit logs, disk snapshots, and memory captures to a WORM S3 bucket with restricted access. Record chain-of-custody and access events for evidence artifacts. Communication: Notify legal and compliance within 2 hours for incidents with potential customer data exposure. Customer notification cadence follows contractual SLAs and regulatory timelines (e.g., GDPR 72-hour window). Post-incident: Conduct a blameless postmortem within 7 days and track action items to closure. Security leads produce an incident summary for compliance evidence.
compliance_evidence_and_workflows: Control mapping: Map system telemetry and docs to common frameworks (ISO27001, SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA as applicable) in the compliance controlbook. Evidence collection workflow: 1) Automated evidence: periodic snapshots of policies, RBAC bindings, encrypted log exports, CI pipeline logs, and release manifests pushed to the evidence repo. 2) Manual evidence: meeting minutes, attestation forms, and exception approvals uploaded by control owners. 3) Evidence retention: store evidence artifacts aligned with audit retention policies (default 7 years for major controls). Audit readiness: Quarterly control reviews with internal auditors. Prepare an audit package with mapping, sample evidence, and test results. Maintain an evidence index with direct links to preserved artifacts and signing metadata.
risk_and_exceptions_process: Purpose: provide a formal process to evaluate and accept residual risk when a control cannot be implemented within required constraints. Process steps: 1) Submit exception request (template below) to security with business justification and compensating controls. 2) Security performs risk assessment and documents expected impact and mitigation plan. 3) Risk committee reviews and either approves (timeboxed) or denies. Approvals must include owner, expiry date, and monitoring requirements. 4) All exceptions are logged and reviewed at least every 30 days until remediated. Exception request template (fields): requester, service, control impacted, justification, compensating controls, proposed expiry, reviewer notes.
appendices_and_checklists: Quick checklist for new production service onboard: IdP integration configured and test SSO completed; RBAC roles defined and least-privilege verified; Audit logging enabled and sample logs validated in central pipeline; Data residency requirements captured and storage configured; KMS keys provisioned and rotation policy defined; CI gates (SAST/SCA/secret-scan) enabled; Release runbook and rollback plan documented. Key metrics and SLOs (security-relevant): privileged-access-review-compliance: 100% quarterly; audit-log-forwarding-availability: 99.9%; incident-detection-mean-time: < 30 minutes (target).
